key_insight: A surrogate-assisted inverse-design workflow can efficiently tune an all-oxide grating emitter to achieve high, narrowband thermal emission matched to TPV cell needs.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more temperature-stable alternative to metal-based emitters for thermophotovoltaic systems, with direct relevance to high-temperature spectral control.
method: Train ExtraTrees surrogate models on FDTD-generated spectra from varied ITO/Al2O3 thicknesses and grating periods
Run Bayesian optimization on a penalty-augmented objective enforcing E_peak > 0.90 while minimizing FWHM and maximizing in-band emission fraction
Validate the optimized design with full FDTD simulations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimization against a multi-metric FOM including peak emissivity, peak wavelength, FWHM, and in-band fraction, with final predictions confirmed by FDTD.
watch_item: Surrogate predictions may be sensitive to the quality and coverage of the FDTD training set, so out-of-distribution geometries could reduce reliability.
paper_title: Surrogate-Assisted Inverse Design and Temperature-Dependent Electrothermal Analysis of an All-Oxide Narrowband Thermophotovoltaic Emitter
